name: Ipili
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Ingemann, Frances. 1980. Vowel harmony and vowel raising in Ipili. (also Ingemann 1996, Ipili finite verb forms; Ingemann's Ipili dictionary materials, U. Kansas)
earlier_scan.note: Ingemann's Ipili phonology papers plausibly state stress; not online-accessible (KU repository 403)

sources.citation: Ingemann, Frances. 1999. Uneventful -ne in Ipili. Kansas Working Papers in Linguistics 24.
sources.note: Third of Ingemann's Ipili papers at KU ScholarWorks; morphosyntactic by title but may carry a transcription/phonology note.

sources.citation: Ingemann, Frances. 1996. Ipili finite verb forms. 1996 Mid-America Linguistics Conference Papers, 209-221. Lawrence, KS: University of Kansas Linguistics Department.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Widener Library, call number P21.M5x 1982); the library holds the journal volume but the item itself was not found; ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.note: Glottolog's only descriptive record for ipil1240; a 13-page morphology paper that may open with orthography/phonology notes (Wikipedia cites it for the absence of consonant clusters).

sources.citation: Wikipedia. Ipili language (article and raw wikitext, accessed 2026-09-17).
sources.note: Five vowels, thirteen consonants, vowel height harmony, no consonant clusters; 'It is reported that Ipili may have tonal contrasts' citing Ingemann 1980 and Franklin 1997. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. 2024 (page modified 2024-06-25). Ipili. New Guinea World, Santa Fe Institute.
sources.note: Phonology section reads in full: 'There is no published phonology of Ipili.' Sources listed: Franklin 1974 (15 reflexes), Franklin 1975 (94 reflexes). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Borchard, Terrance & Philip Gibbs. 2011. Parallelism and Poetics in Tindi Narratives Sung in the Ipili Language. In Rumsey & Niles (eds.), Sung Tales from the Papua New Guinea Highlands, 165-195. Canberra: ANU E Press. doi:10.22459/stpngh.08.2011.08
sources.note: Nothing on stress, tone or accent (chapter a full-text search for stress/accent/phonolog: no hits); poetics and parallelism only.

sources.citation: Ingemann, Frances. 2011. The Structure of Chanted Ipili Tindi. In Alan Rumsey & Don Niles (eds.), Sung Tales from the Papua New Guinea Highlands, 197-206. Canberra: ANU E Press. doi:10.22459/stpngh.08.2011.09
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p.198 n.2: transcription follows Borchard's orthography; 'there is no vowel length distinction in Ipili'. p.202 n.7 (on Praat pitch traces of chant lines): 'There may also be other fluctuations attributable to lexical tone, which has not been fully analysed and is not marked in the transcription.' Chant pitch: 'The chant typically begins with a rising pitch on the first syllable' (p.201) - a chant-melody property, not word stress.

sources.citation: Niles, Don & Alan Rumsey. 2011. Introducing Highlands Sung Tales. In Rumsey & Niles (eds.), Sung Tales from the Papua New Guinea Highlands, 1-38. Canberra: ANU E Press.
sources.note: p.15: 'Furthermore, Ipili also has a word-tone system, like Huli and other members of the Engan group of languages described below. But whether this melodic movement is dictated by speech-tone or is independent of it is not known.' Second-hand (ethnomusicological intro); no mention of stress.

downloaded and a full-text search for stress/accent Ipili/Ingemann in the hope that the 1980 or 1996 papers were reprinted there: no Ipili content in any volume (vol. 5(1) is a modality issue). Files not retained.

sources.citation: Ingemann, Frances. 1980. Vowel harmony and vowel raising in Ipili. 1980 Mid-America Linguistics Conference Papers, 251-256. Lawrence, KS: University of Kansas Linguistics Department.
sources.note: The only published phonological paper on Ipili (6 pp.); Wikipedia cites it for possible tonal contrasts, so it presumably contains a phoneme inventory and suprasegmental remarks; an earlier compilation also named it. KU ScholarWorks blocks our network (not reachable by automated download); no archived copy at the Internet Archive.

sources.citation: Franklin, Karl J. 1975. Comments on Proto-Engan. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study, Vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 263-275. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Comparative/lexicostatistical; Ipili appears in the Proto-Engan reflex lists (pp. 263, 291; pp. 307, 335) and in Wurm's classification table (p. 513). No statement about Ipili stress or tone.

sources.citation: Franklin, Karl J. 1997. Engan pronouns and their old endings. Australian Journal of Linguistics 17(2): 185-217.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Comparative Engan article cited by Wikipedia together with Ingemann 1980 for Ipili tonal contrasts; Franklin's Engan comparative work sometimes summarises each language's phonology including tone/stress.

sources.citation: Ingemann, Frances. 1968. The linguistic structure of an Ipili-Paiyala song type. Proceedings, 8th International Congress of Anthropological and Ethnological Sciences, Tokyo and Kyoto, vol. 2: Ethnology, 398-400. Tokyo: Science Council of Japan.
